_note: ⛔ SNG-403. LOCAL LAYOUTS. Erik: 'the docks in millbrook on the river, the smithy, the fields.' ⚠️ THE TERRAIN GENERATOR HAS NOTHING AT THIS SCALE — its finest feature is ~0.3° ≈ 33 km and a village spans ~0.01° ≈ 1 km. So a local map is NOT a further zoom of the world raster; it is a NEW layer. ⛔ BUT IT IS NOT INVENTED EITHER: the world layer supplies the DIRECTIONS, and everything here is placed against them. That is the pattern the detailing engine should learn.
_frame: `localMap: {bearing, metres}` from the settlement centre. Bearing 0 = toward the pole (up-map), 90 = east. ⚠️ METRES, not degrees — a village is 400-800 m across and degrees at that scale are unreadable. The engine converts: dLat = metres·cos(bearing)/111320, dLon = metres·sin(bearing)/(111320·cos(lat)).
_derivation: ⛔ THE THREE GRADIENTS THE WORLD ALREADY KNOWS, measured at each settlement: (1) RIVER BEARING and distance — from the traced hydrology; (2) UPHILL BEARING — sample the generator's raw elevation around the point; (3) ROAD BEARINGS — from connections' worldPos. ⚠️ Water trades go riverward. Terraces and orchards go uphill. Fields take the flat. Gates and markets sit on the road bearings. Everything else fills the middle.

millbrook._reading: Its own seed names them and nobody made them places: 'Water wheels turn along the Echo River; terraced gardens climb the lower slopes. THE VILLAGE WELL AND THE RIVER DOCK ARE THE TWO CENTRES of daily life.' ⛔ Two centres is a LAYOUT INSTRUCTION and it has been sitting in the prose.

sites.name: The Village Well
sites.why: ⛔ One of the two centres the seed names. It IS the centre — bearing and distance zero.

sites.name: The River Dock
sites.why: ⛔ The other centre. ON THE RIVER BEARING — the one placement the world layer dictates outright.

sites.name: The Water Wheels
sites.why: Downstream of the dock on the same water. ⚠️ Wheels go below the landing so the boats are not fighting the race.

sites.name: The Terraced Gardens
sites.why: ⛔ 'Climb the lower slopes' — placed on the MEASURED UPHILL BEARING, not a guess.

sites.name: The Irrigation Fields
sites.why: ⚠️ The flat: opposite the uphill, and off the river so the ditches can run TO them. The encounterFlavor is farmers arguing about irrigation shares — this is what they are arguing over.

sites.name: The Smithy
sites.why: On the road out to Echo River Crossing. ⚠️ A smith sits where the carts already stop, and near enough the water to quench.

sites.name: Mara Wells' Store
sites.why: ⛔ ALREADY A PLACE, promoted from play, and sitting at Millbrook's EXACT coordinates — CCode's 'a room's position is a duplicate' finding, live. Now it stands between the well and the road, which is where a village store stands.

sites.name: The Commons
sites.why: Between the well and the dock — the ground people cross going from one centre to the other, which is what a commons IS.

echo_river_crossing._dataFlag: ⛔ ITS NEAREST TRACED RIVER IS 3.83° AWAY — about 425 km — AND ITS ENTIRE IDENTITY IS A BRIDGE OVER THE ECHO. `waterauth.json` authors a river here and the built hydrology does not carry one to it. ⚠️ I am placing the bridge on the fiction, not on the measurement, and flagging the gap rather than quietly bending the layout around bad data. SNG-403b.

sites.name: The Stone-and-Cable Bridge
sites.why: ⛔ The town IS the bridge. Centre by definition; everything else is which END you are on.

sites.name: The Old Bridge-Stone
sites.why: 'The old bridge-stone at the crossing is a waygate, and the least ceremonious one in the world — carters queue behind it.' ⚠️ A QUEUE IS A PLACEMENT: it sits at the bridge mouth, not off to one side.

sites.name: The Carters' Queue
sites.why: ⛔ On the Millbrook road bearing — the queue forms along the road people arrive by.

sites.name: The Empty Fisher Shacks
sites.why: ⚠️ 'Fisher shacks stand empty' — riverward and UPSTREAM, where the contamination is worst. They are empty for a reason and the position says why.

sites.name: The Granite Shoulders
sites.why: On the measured uphill — 'where the river narrows between granite shoulders'.

sites.name: The Survey Camp
sites.why: ⚠️ Contamination teams from Heights and Plateau, camped apart from the town and from each other.

greyhearth._reading: 'A town that buries for every road that meets here — the Crossing's dead and the Palelands' both.' ⛔ A BURYING TOWN'S LAYOUT IS ITS TRAFFIC: the dead arrive by road and go uphill.

sites.name: The Receiving Yard
sites.why: ⛔ On the Crossing road. The dead arrive from where the roads meet, so the yard faces that way.

sites.name: The Burying Grounds
sites.why: ⛔ UPHILL, on the measured bearing — drainage. Every real burying ground sits above its town.

sites.name: The Grey Hearth
sites.why: The town's name and its centre — the fire that gives the trades their work.

sites.name: The Singers' Hall
sites.why: 'Everyone here has sung over one.' ⚠️ Between the hearth and the grounds — on the walk.

sites.name: The Quiet Road
sites.why: ⛔ On the bearing to the Quiet Ground, which is where the dying go BEFORE. The two towns are one process.

the_cogitarium._verticalFinding: ⛔ THIS ONE BREAKS THE HORIZONTAL FRAME AND IT SHOULD. Its two promoted places are an ENTRANCE HALL and a THIRD TERRACE — the same footprint at different heights. ⚠️ AN INTERIOR NEEDS A VERTICAL AXIS. `localMap` needs an optional `level`: 0 ground, positive up, negative below. Without it the Cogitarium's two rooms land on top of each other and the map says they are the same place.

sites.name: Cogitarium Entrance Hall
sites.why: ⛔ On the Middle Way road bearing — an entrance faces the road people arrive by. Ground level.

sites.name: Cogitarium Third Terrace
sites.why: ⛔ LEVEL 3 — it is the THIRD terrace and the name says so. Uphill side, because a terrace climbs the slope it is cut into.

_generalisation: ⛔ EIGHT LAYOUTS, 38 SITES, AND THE RULE SET GREW BY MEASURING RATHER THAN BY GUESSING. The four Valley towns gave: water trades riverward, terraces uphill, fields on the flat, markets on the roads. The four contrast towns broke that usefully — ⚠️ GREYWATER (relief 0.002) proved UPHILL IS NOISE ON FLAT GROUND; ⚠️ KINDLEROW (relief 0.541, no water within 9°) is the mirror, and its cistern EXISTS BECAUSE THE TERRAIN FORCED IT; ⛔ THE SERVICE WAYS broke the horizontal frame entirely — a tunnel network has depth, not a radius; ⚠️ THE FIGURE WORKS had NO strong gradient at all, and there the TRADITION carried the layout. ⛔ THAT IS THE ENGINE'S PRECEDENCE ORDER: strong gradient first, tradition aesthetic second, and never free invention.

greywater_stilts._ruleFinding: ⛔ RELIEF 0.002 — DEAD FLAT. 'Uphill' is a MEANINGLESS AXIS here and the engine must not use it: bearing 90 is noise, not a slope. ⚠️ THE ORGANISING AXIS IS THE WATER — the marsh is 0.37° away and the town stands ON it. New rule: WHEN RELIEF < ~0.05, DROP THE UPHILL GRADIENT AND ORGANISE ON WATER AND ROADS. Millbrook's terraces exist because Millbrook has a slope; here there is nothing to climb.

sites.name: The Main Platform
sites.why: ⛔ A stilt town has no ground, so its centre is a BUILT thing. The largest platform is the square.

sites.name: The Rope-Walks
sites.why: 'Rope-walks lace between platforms.' ⚠️ NOT A PLACE SO MUCH AS THE STREETS — laced between, so placed between the platforms rather than at a point.

sites.name: The Skiff Landing
sites.why: ⛔ On the ROAD bearing, not the water bearing — in a marsh town the skiffs ARE the road, so the landing faces where travellers come from.

sites.name: The Deep Platforms
sites.why: ⚠️ 'Whoever else needed somewhere the aligned powers don't reach' — furthest from the roads, which is the whole reason those people are there.

sites.name: The Pole Yard
sites.why: ⛔ A stilt town's only real industry is REPLACING ITS OWN LEGS. Nobody wrote this down; the town's existence requires it.

kindlerow._ruleFinding: ⚠️ RELIEF 0.541 — the STEEPEST of the eight, and no water within 9°. ⛔ THE MIRROR OF GREYWATER: here uphill is the dominant axis and water is unusable. The Kindlespine runs behind the town (SNG-393). A forge town with no river gets its water from the hill, which is a fact the layout should state.

sites.name: The Row
sites.why: ⛔ The town is a ROW and the name says so — forges strung along the Crossing road, not clustered round a square.

sites.name: The Assay House
sites.why: 'Tells you honestly what your metal is worth.' ⚠️ At the road end where metal ARRIVES — you are assayed before you are sold to.

sites.name: The Lamp-Makers' Sheds
sites.why: ⛔ On the road to the Blaze. Lamps go where the light doctrine is, and Kindlerow sells to them without joining them.

sites.name: The Charcoal Slope
sites.why: ⛔ Uphill on the measured bearing — fuel comes down to a forge, never up.

sites.name: The Catch-Cistern
sites.why: ⚠️ NO RIVER WITHIN 9°, AND A FORGE MUST QUENCH. Uphill catchment is the only honest answer; the terrain forced this one into existence.

the_service_ways._ruleFinding: ⛔ THIS ONE BREAKS THE HORIZONTAL FRAME ENTIRELY. 'Precursor tunnels… THEY RUN UNDER EVERYTHING — under the Gearlands, under the Valley, under places the Wrights have not admitted to.' ⚠️ A TUNNEL NETWORK IS NOT A TOWN WITH A CENTRE. Its extent is measured in DAYS, not metres, and its axis is DEPTH. This is the second vertical case after the Cogitarium and it is a stronger one: `localMap.level` is not optional, and for places like this `radiusMetres` is the wrong unit.
the_service_ways.extentNote: unbounded — the seed says it is not fully mapped after four centuries

sites.name: The Pressureholt Stair
sites.why: ⛔ The way in from above, on the Pressureholt road bearing. Level −1: you go DOWN to enter.

sites.name: The Mapped Reach
sites.why: 'Mapped for four centuries.' ⚠️ The part they will show you, running toward the Axis Gate.

sites.name: The Unadmitted Ways
sites.why: ⛔ 'Under places the Wrights have not admitted to.' Deep, far, and deliberately vague — ⚠️ the position is a CLAIM ABOUT SECRECY, and metres here are a shrug rather than a measurement.

the_figure_works._ruleFinding: ⚠️ ONE ROAD OUT, middling relief, no water. ⛔ WHEN THE GRADIENTS ARE ALL WEAK THE TRADITION HAS TO CARRY THE LAYOUT — and for the Figurists that is legible: they are geometric, so the town is laid out ON a figure. This is the case where the engine should fall back to the TRADITION'S AESTHETIC rather than inventing terrain reasons.

sites.name: The Working Hall
sites.why: 'Where symbols are made that ACT.' The centre of the figure, because a figure has one.

sites.name: The Proving Yard
sites.why: ⛔ 'The meanings do exactly what they mean, which is not always what was wanted.' A yard at a THIRD of the circle — you test a made meaning away from where you made it.

sites.name: The Containment Figures
sites.why: ⛔ The other third. 'The entire history of this people's disasters' — this is where the disasters are kept, and its position completes the triangle.

sites.name: The Cloudform Gate
sites.why: The single road out. ⚠️ One road means one gate, and its bearing is not a choice.

_basisNote: ⛔ SNG-404 §2 asked CCode to tune the relief threshold against these eight layouts. ⚠️ MY OWN DATA COULD NOT ANSWER IT AND I HAD TO FIX THE DATA FIRST. I recorded intent in PROSE (`why`) and nothing machine-readable, so 'did this site use the uphill gradient?' could only be guessed by comparing bearings — and that guess is wrong: Greywater's skiff landing sits at bearing 85 against a noise-uphill of 90, so it READS as uphill-placed when it was placed on the ROAD. ⛔ AT RELIEF 0.002 THE UPHILL BEARING IS NOISE, AND NOISE COINCIDES WITH THINGS. `basis` now states which gradient decided each placement: river | uphill | anti-uphill | road | anti-road | between | prose | tradition | inferred. THE THRESHOLD IS TUNABLE FROM THIS FIELD, not from bearing arithmetic.
